transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Three Republican representatives say that former NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang will testify
before Congress on Tuesday, December 1, behind closed doors.
NVIDIA's top lawyer will do the same the following day.
Lawmakers want to know more about how NVIDIA computer chips were sold to a foreign company
once led by a woman who was suspected of spying for China.
The reports say Huang was involved in an affair with her.
Separately, the Trump administration has issued a new rule closing a loophole on how certain
foreign countries and companies can buy and use U.S. computer chips.
Trump administration officials are calling on Congress to give them $50 billion to finish
upgrading the nation's air traffic control system.
This follows last Friday's national ground stop that snarled air travel.
Democrats are skeptical.
Rhode Island Senator Jack Reed says the Trump administration has not properly spent the
money Congress already gave them for upgrades.
Yes, we have to improve the system.
It has been neglected over time, and we hope, and frankly, that they would have prioritized
the money that we gave to them, the $12 billion in the big beautiful bill and made much more
progress and do it in a way that wouldn't have been disrupted.
He spoke to NPR's "Morning Edition."
Ukraine struck a strategic bridge linking mainland Russia to the annexed Crimean Peninsula
for the second time in as many days.
Ukraine says the attack is retaliatory for Russia's own targeting of Ukrainian bridges
and other civilian infrastructure, and piers Charles Maine's reports from Moscow.
Ukraine has previously attempted attacks along the 12-mile Kerch Bridge, seeing it as both
the physical symbol of Russia's illegal annexation of Crimea in 2014 and a pet project of President
Vladimir Putin.
Yet early Tuesday, according to Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky, a Ukrainian-made
Flamingo missile pierced Russia's air defenses to inflict heavy damage on the structure,
destroying a key support archway and sending a section of road into the sea.
The Moscow-backed authorities in Crimea said two people were killed as a result and ordered
all car traffic across the bridge halted.
The Kremlin spokesman said President Putin had been informed of the attack and vowed
to rebuild the bridge better and stronger than before.
Charles Maine's NPR News, Moscow.
The federal government is going to conduct a nationwide test today of its emergency alert
system.
This will include TV, radio and satellite providers, but it will not include your cell
phone.
The emergency test will start at 2.20 p.m. Eastern time, which means at 11.20 a.m. Pacific
time.
Regular programming will be interrupted for this test message.
No action or response is needed by the public.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
The Pan American Health Organization is scheduled to announce whether measles has again become
endemic in the United States.
Scientists believe the answer is yes.
The organization will determine whether the U.S. will lose its official designation as
a country that has eliminated measles.
In Sudan, archaeologists have discovered the original floor of a medieval cathedral dating
back more than a thousand years.
Historians say the church is one of the most important Christian buildings in Africa's
history, as NPR's Jule Bright reports.
Researchers say the Great Church of Jesus was the largest and most important church
in Medivhia Macuria, one of the early Christian kingdoms that emerged along the Nile River
in Northern Africa following the arrival of Christian missionaries in the sixth century.
The site of the church was first discovered by a team of Polish and Sudanese archaeologists
in 2021, but the cathedral's massive walls made excavation challenging.
The excavating team says they removed substantial layers of accumulated debris before they reached
the cathedral's original levels.
Researchers say the cathedral could have influenced the development of religious architecture
across Africa in the same way Istanbul's Hagia Sophia influenced religious architecture
across Europe and the rest of the world.
Jule Bright, NPR News, Vegas.
Motoring Club AAA says 81.5 million Americans will travel over Thanksgiving this year.
That's a slight dip from last year when 81.6 million traveled.
AAA is citing higher travel costs.
This is NPR News.
